new_statements.quote: [5.1.1] ... Chaque voyelle dans la syllabe porte un des quatre tons distinctifs, [ton 1] tres haut, ton 2 haut, ton 3 moyen et ton 4 bas. Ce dernier se realise au niveau bas sauf quand il se trouve en finale d'un monosyllabe devant pause ou il se realise par un ton descendant a partir du niveau bas. Remarquons que les voyelles fermees /u/ et /i/ ne portent que tres rarement un ton 2 ... [2.1.1] D'une maniere generale, le mot phonologique simple est caracterise par l'harmonie vocalique (cf. 6.3.2.2.). D'autre part, il constitue le domaine d'extension de sequences tonales bien determinees (cf. 5.1.1.).
new_statements.translation: [5.1.1] Every vowel in the syllable carries one of the four distinctive tones: [tone 1] extra-high, tone 2 high, tone 3 mid and tone 4 low. The latter is realised at low level except when final in a monosyllable before pause, where it is realised as a fall from low level. Note that the close vowels /u/ and /i/ only very rarely bear tone 2 ... [2.1.1] In general the simple phonological word is characterised by vowel harmony; it also constitutes the domain over which well-defined tone sequences extend.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nyabwa is described as a four-level tone language (extra-high, high, mid, low), every vowel bearing a tone and the phonological word being the domain of tone patterns and vowel harmony; the monograph has no accent/stress section (TOC) and no occurrence of 'accent'/'accentuation'/'intensite' in its full-text index, i.e. no statement on word stress. The Kru family survey (Marchese 1983, sec. 2.4.5) adds that distinctive accent has so far been reported only for Grebo among Kru languages.
new_statements.exceptions: none regarding stress; tonal detail only (tone 4 falls before pause in monosyllables; close vowels rarely bear tone 2, lax mid vowels rarely tone 1).
new_statements.domain_note: phonological word (mot phonologique simple) is the stated domain of tone sequences and vowel harmony; citation forms with numeric tone marking 1-4.
new_statements.identity_note: Bentinck 1978 describes Nyabwa proper as spoken around Guessabo (sous-prefecture de Zoukougbeu); she treats Nyedebwa (Vavoua, north) as the only notable dialect variant (100% intercomprehension) and mentions the Kouzie canton (Buyo) separately. Allou 2017/2019 describes Kouzie, which Glottolog Falle's articles are based on Zoukougbeu and Iboguhe speakers. All are nyab1255; no sub-glottocodes involved.
